# docs: add ownership guidance to house rules and the PR procedure

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Write down where each kind of code belongs, so contributors and agents put new code in the right
place without having to ask.

## Why

The upcoming restructuring moves code between owners. Unless the rules explain the reasoning,
later changes will drift back to the old layout.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Target responsibilities", "Error ownership and technical failure handling",
"House rules and review".

- `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`, `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`,
  `.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md`: add short ownership guidance with concrete examples:
  - CLI does not receive a container or cradle; it calls an application operation and presents the result.
  - Configurable defaults (for example the step retry count) are not domain rules; domain consumes
    resolved `RunSettings`.
  - A capability failure (storage, Git, sandbox) belongs with its port contract, not in domain just
    because several modules return it.
  - Composition only wires: it chooses implementations and starts the executable, and makes no
    resume, retry, locking or publication decisions.
- `.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a PR that changes
  ownership states the owner, why the concept belongs there, and whether it introduces a pattern
  agents should copy. Add this to the existing procedure; do not create a parallel guide.
- Also update `.agents/` copies of these rules or skills if they exist and are tracked.

This issue changes documentation only. Do not move code, and do not enforce ownership through
names (such as `DEFAULT_*`) or tests that check prose.

## Done when

- [ ] The rules above carry the four examples, each in the rule that owns it.
- [ ] The PR procedure and template ask for an ownership rationale.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` pass.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/54

docs.design:
# Goal

Add concise ownership guidance to the existing house rules and PR procedure so contributors and agents can place new code by responsibility. This is a documentation-only change.

# Context

The requested guidance spans five existing files:

| Requested guidance | Current implementation and documentation owner |
| --- | --- |
| CLI calls application operations and presents results without receiving a container or cradle | `src/cli/app-action.ts`, `with-app.ts`, and command handlers currently expose containers or cradle access. `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md` owns encapsulation guidance, but its good example accesses `app.cradle`. |
| Composition only wires implementations and starts the executable | `src/app/container.ts` currently combines construction with scopes, cleanup, and retry execution. The callee-ownership rule names this file as the composition root and assigns it lifetime decisions. |
| Config owns configurable defaults; domain consumes resolved settings | `src/domain/settings.ts` currently contains `RunSettings`, retry defaults, and domain stopping rules. `.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md` owns parsing guidance, but broadly assigns schemas to domain and shows an application operation accepting `AwilixContainer`. |
| Capability failures belong with port contracts | `src/domain/errors.ts` currently centralizes business and technical failures. `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md` explicitly directs new failures there, while correctly assigning raw exception translation to adapters. |
| Ownership changes explain their rationale and reusable patterns | `.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md` requires every PR-template section to be filled. `.github/pull_request_template.md` already has a technical **How** section suitable for this requirement. |

The authority is `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`, particularly Target responsibilities, Error ownership and technical failure handling, and House rules and review. `docs/architecture.html` documents the current implementation. No tracked `.agents/` copies exist.

# Chosen approach

Revise the existing guidance in place, replacing contradictory instructions and examples instead of appending competing rules.

In callee ownership, state that CLI receives bound application operations, calls them with parsed input, and presents their results. It receives neither a container nor a cradle. Replace the good cradle-access example with an illustrative operation call that exposes no construction details. Preserve lifecycle encapsulation, while distinguishing application-owned sequencing and resource-lifetime policy from composition-supplied construction and capabilities. Composition chooses implementations, wires dependencies and reporting, and starts the executable; it makes no resume, retry, locking, or publication decisions.

In edge parsing, qualify schema ownership by meaning: domain owns business types and invariants; config owns configuration schemas, defaults, and resolution policy. Use the step retry count as the configurable-default example. Domain consumes resolved `RunSettings`, including when comparing review cycles against the configured cap. Genuine safety and stopping rules remain domain rules; numeric constants are not automatically settings. Replace container-bearing operation examples with typed, container-free examples while retaining parse-once guidance.

In error guidance, replace the blanket instruction to add failures to `src/domain/errors.ts`. Business failures belong in domain; portable storage, Git, and sandbox failures belong with their port contracts even when several modules return them. Adapters translate raw library exceptions into those declared failures. Keep definitions singular and contracts narrow. Preserve expected-failure `Result` semantics, panic behavior, cleanup semantics, and reporting guidance. Do not prescribe a new shared error registry or relocate existing helpers.

Extend the existing PR procedure and the template's **How** guidance with the same conditional requirement: when ownership changes, state the owner, why the concept belongs there, and whether the change introduces a reusable pattern agents should copy. Ownership remains a reviewer judgment.

The target differs from today's implementation: CLI exposes containers, composition and lifecycle policy are mixed in app, retry defaults live in domain, and technical failures are centralized there. The spec also selects a dedicated composition owner, whereas existing guidance names `src/app/container.ts` and `AGENTS.md` restricts Awilix to app. Document the target responsibilities without claiming files have moved or changing the current Awilix restriction. Construction choices remain deferred to spike #49. Record this distinction in the implementation PR; no request-versus-spec conflict was found for this documentation scope.

# Alternatives considered

1. **Append ownership bullets while retaining existing examples.** Rejected because contributors would still encounter good examples that teach cradle access and an instruction to put all failures in domain.
2. **Create a separate ownership guide and link it from the rules.** Rejected because it duplicates policy and violates the request to extend the existing procedure.
3. **Implement the ownership moves alongside the documentation.** Rejected because source relocation, dependency enforcement, and construction changes belong to the broader refactor and exceed this documentation-only request.

# Assumptions

- The spec governs target ownership; current code and architecture maps remain accurate descriptions of the implementation until their respective refactor slices land.
- Examples illustrate contracts without committing to new public API names or a construction mechanism.
- No tracked `.agents/` mirrors require updates; recheck before implementation.
- The required checks for this slice are `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint`.

# Non-goals

No runtime changes, code moves, new configuration options, changed defaults, error-contract changes, scanners, naming-based enforcement, or prose tests. Do not select Awilix versus explicit factories, add a parallel guide, update versions, or create release tags. Preserve sandbox-only agent execution, credential protections, target-tree isolation, and all observable command and recovery behavior.

# Affected areas

- `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`
- `.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md`
- `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`
- `.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md`
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`

Architecture maps, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` remain unchanged because no implementation ownership or paths move.
docs.plan:
## Step 1 — Confirm scope and reconcile existing guidance

Read `AGENTS.md`, applicable house rules, `docs/architecture.html`, and the three named spec sections. Inspect the current CLI/container boundary, settings defaults, and error definitions to distinguish target guidance from current implementation. Confirm tracked `.agents/` mirrors with `git ls-files`. Keep changes scoped to the five requested documents unless tracked mirrors are discovered.

## Step 2 — Update ownership rules and their examples together

Revise callee ownership to require container-free CLI calls into application operations and composition-only wiring. Replace contradictory good examples and distinguish application lifetime policy from supplied construction capabilities.

Revise edge parsing to assign configuration schemas and configurable defaults to config while retaining domain-owned business schemas, resolved `RunSettings`, and genuine safety rules. Use step retry count as the concrete example and remove container-bearing application signatures from the parsing examples.

Revise error guidance to assign failures by meaning, explicitly placing storage, Git, and sandbox capability failures with port contracts. Remove the blanket domain-error placement instruction. Preserve adapter exception translation, narrow failure unions, and existing Result/panic and cleanup guidance. Do not move source or invent replacement modules.

## Step 3 — Add ownership rationale to the existing PR workflow

Extend the commit-pr procedure and the template's **How** instructions to require the owner, the reason the concept belongs there, and whether the change establishes a pattern agents should copy whenever ownership changes. Retain existing template sections and verification requirements. Update tracked mirrors only if any are found.

## Step 4 — Review consistency and validate the documentation change

Review the full diff against the four required examples and the spec. Check that each example appears in its owning rule, surrounding examples no longer contradict it, and wording does not claim the broader refactor is implemented. Confirm no runtime files, architecture maps, dependency policy, or public behavior changed.

Run `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` using the repository's supported runtime. Correct formatting in affected documents and rerun checks as needed. Add no prose tests or source scanners. Report actual results and any blockers; do not claim checks were run during this design step. In the implementation PR, explain the distinction between target ownership guidance and the unchanged current layout, and record any spec-driven deviation.

slices.title: docs(agents): align ownership rules and PR rationale
slices.description: Implements plan steps 1-4. Reconcile the applicable rules, architecture, three named spec sections, and current implementation, then update the five requested documents and any tracked .agents mirrors as one coherent guidance change. Require container-free CLI application calls and composition-only wiring; assign configuration schemas and configurable defaults to config, using step retry count as the example; assign storage, Git, and sandbox capability failures to their port contracts by meaning. Correct surrounding examples while preserving domain business schemas, resolved RunSettings, safety rules, and Result/panic, narrow-union, adapter translation, and cleanup guidance. Require ownership changes to explain their owner, rationale, and whether they establish a pattern agents should copy in both commit-pr and the template's How instructions. Review all four required examples and distinguish target guidance from the unchanged implementation. Keep runtime files, architecture maps, dependency policy, and public behavior unchanged. Run format:check and lint with the supported runtime, fix affected formatting, and report actual results, blockers, and any spec-driven deviation without adding prose tests or source scanners. These edits belong together because the ownership rules, examples, and review requirements must communicate one consistent standard.
